data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于历史实验和社会学视角的分析，以及对特定历史航行实验的质疑和补充说明。

不同观点：
• rage4774 认为当前的实验和结论过于自信，仅提供了在当前时间点上看似合理的路线，而忽略了社会学视角。他举了古罗马斯多葛学派的例子，指出历史上有些人基于特定信仰和价值观做出看似“非自然”的行为，因此当前的结论可能只是浅显的回应，无法排除其他可能性，不能让人确信历史事实。

• raincom 没有提出具体观点，仅提供了一个链接，可能意在引导读者查看更多相关信息或参考资料。

• notfed 对实验的具体细节提出疑问，特别是航行实验的起止点以及如何确定旅行是故意进行的，质疑实验的证据和结论的可靠性。

• flowmerchant 补充了关于女性在耐力划船活动中优势的讨论。他以德州水上挑战赛为例，指出女性在长时间划船中具有更低的重心和更强的心理耐力，这与实验中使用女性划船的选择相符。

补充讨论：
• rage4774 强调了社会学和历史价值观对人们行为的影响，提出了实验结论可能存在的不确定性。
• notfed 对实验的地理和证据细节提出了具体疑问，要求更明确的说明。
• flowmerchant 提供了关于女性在划船活动中表现的实证支持，补充了实验设计中性别选择的合理性。

争议焦点：
• rage4774 对实验结论的可靠性和全面性提出质疑，认为缺少社会学视角的考量。
• notfed 对实验的具体实施细节和证据的充分性表示怀疑。

这些讨论共同构成了对历史实验的多角度审视，包括方法论、性别角色以及结论的可靠性等问题。

data.title: What LLMs Know About Their Users
data.author: voxleone
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了如果在海边发现鱿鱼的“卵团”该如何处理。作者提供了相关建议，并提到读者也可以在这篇关于鱿鱼的文章下讨论其他未涉及的安全新闻。文章还包括博客的管理政策，并标记了发布日期和相关标签，目前有14条评论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：本地LLM（大型语言模型）的隐私与数据安全问题，以及用户对LLM了解其个人信息的担忧。

不同观点：
• **对本地LLM使用的质疑**：drillsteps5认为，除非从事非法或不道德行为，否则没有理由使用本地LLM。该评论暗示使用本地LLM可能与不良意图相关。
• **对LLM了解用户信息的担忧**：多位用户（如rcruzeiro, b0a04gl, bgwalter）表示对LLM能够获取用户个人信息的担忧，尤其是当这些信息被用于调整模型输出时。bgwalter甚至将这种情况比作FBI档案。
• **LLM不获取个人信息的声明**：BurningFrog和holri通过实际测试（使用Grok和Mistral.ai）表明，这些模型并不直接获取个人信息，除非用户明确分享这些信息。
• **对LLM隐私风险的理性分析**：nullc指出，人们在LLM时代对隐私的期望往往不准确，LLM可能会通过“推理”得出错误结论，这增加了隐私风险。
• **隐私保护解决方案的建议**：nonelog提出使用Duck.ai这样的平台，完全保护隐私，不收集用户数据。
• **对LLM隐私问题的接受与适应**：EGreg表示，对LLM构建用户画像的情况是可控的，且与在公共社交媒体上的行为类似，强调用户自我警觉。

补充讨论：
• **LLM输出个性化的技术原理**：b0a04gl提到，LLM能够通过用户历史交互生成嵌入，并通过交叉注意力机制影响输出，即使不显式传递历史聊天内容，模型仍能“记住”用户偏好。
• **对LLM“间谍”角色的调侃**：marcusstorm将LLM比作间谍或FBI特工，暗示其能够揭露用户信息，这与实际LLM行为形成对比。
• **用户对隐私概念的理解差异**：hardlianotion提到对“integrous”一词的不理解，反映出用户在讨论隐私问题时存在概念混淆。
• **LLM隐私与实用性的平衡**：simianwords质疑如果没有LLM了解用户信息，模型的实用性是否会下降，提出了隐私与功能之间的权衡问题。

争议焦点：LLM是否应该以及如何获取和使用用户数据以优化输出，以及用户对隐私保护的期望与现实之间的差距。

data.title: Cell Towers Can Double as Cheap Radar Systems for Ports and Harbors (2014)
data.author: transpute
data.article_summary: 文章报道了细胞塔可以作为低成本的雷达系统，利用其发出的被动无线电信号检测小船，从而提升港口和海港的安全性。这种名为"被动相干定位系统"（Passive Coherent Location）的技术，通过分析手机信号的反射来探测和跟踪船只，无需专门的雷达设备。该技术成本低且易于部署，特别适用于监控大面积水域，为港口安全提供了一种经济有效的解决方案。这项创新展示了通信基础设施在安全领域的潜在新应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用手机信号塔进行被动雷达探测的可行性、优势和潜在问题

不同观点：
• **支持技术创新的观点**：
   - builtsimple指出该技术利用现有的手机信号塔发射信号，几乎不消耗额外能量，且能在海上提供4公里的船只探测范围，非常 impressive。他还提到现代蜂窝基站已经具备波束成形能力，可能无需多个接收站点就能获得不错的方位精度。
   - ChuckMcM认为这是利用环境中已有电磁波信号的创新应用，强调了利用现有信号源（如手机信号塔和WiFi）进行探测的潜力和趣味性。他指出，通过多个基站可以计算出目标的速度和方位。
   - ziofill支持这种工程“黑客”行为，提到他的朋友曾写过一篇论文，探讨如何利用GPS信号作为雷达源。

• **质疑其实际应用和成本效益的观点**：
   - dghlsakjg质疑该系统是否真正解决了实际问题，指出目前用于小型港口或码头的雷达系统价格在2000到5000美元之间，且这些专用雷达系统已经非常成熟。他还担心如果被动信号源失效，系统的可靠性如何保证。
   - ofalkaed也表示怀疑，认为在当前雷达设备已经非常便宜的情况下，是否真的有港口或码头会选择使用手机信号塔进行探测。

• **讨论技术扩展性和潜在风险的观点**：
   - ImPostingOnHN提到有初创公司利用5G信号进行步态识别，表明该技术在安防和监控领域有更广泛的应用。
   - janpmz进一步指出，5G信号不仅可以用于船只探测，还可以用于跟踪街上的行人。
   - nelox提供了关于利用5G信号进行洪水预报的例子，显示出该技术在其他领域的潜在应用。
   - ReptileMan则提出了该技术在军事领域的潜在应用，询问是否可以帮助拦截导弹和无人机。

• **反对和批评的声音**：
   - timewizard认为使用自动识别系统（AIS）更为智能和便捷，暗示该技术可能并不如现有方案有效。
   - soundpuppy指出需求方和技术设计方之间的差距很大，容易导致腐败问题，暗示技术应用过程中可能面临管理和利益问题。

补充讨论：
• **对成本的敏感性**：dostick对讨论中频繁出现的“廉价”描述提出质疑，认为并非所有事情都需要围绕金钱展开。
• **多路径干扰问题**：builtsimple提到在城市环境中多路径干扰是一个重大挑战，但水面对信号的反射相对均匀，可能更适合这种技术的应用。

争议焦点：
• 该技术是否真正具备成本效益和实用性，尤其是在已经有成熟且价格合理的传统雷达系统的情况下。
• 该技术在隐私和安全方面的潜在风险，尤其是在行人跟踪和识别等应用中。

data.title: Anticheat Update Tracking
data.author: not-matthias
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者对反作弊系统（特别是EasyAntiCheat）更新追踪的研究。EasyAntiCheat在被Epic Games收购前后，通过不同CDN分发更新，更新URL结构有所变化。作者通过逆向工程和二进制分析，研究如何解密其更新模块，找到解密算法并将加密数据转换为PE文件。然而，该文件还被VMProtect保护，进一步分析需要脱壳。文章概述了作者的研究过程和发现，包括对不同反作弊系统的更新追踪方法的总结。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏反作弊系统的有效性、安全性及其对用户隐私和系统的影响

不同观点：
• nulld3v对BattleEye反作弊系统的信任提出质疑，提到该系统曾有漏洞，黑客可以利用该漏洞随意永久封禁任何玩家。他质疑为什么还要信任这些反作弊系统。
• rak提到ESEA曾经在其客户端中捆绑比特币挖矿程序，进一步引发对反作弊系统供应商的信任问题。
• varun_ch建议游戏开发者应限制客户端可访问的数据量，将更多游戏逻辑放在服务器端处理，以减少作弊的可能性。他质疑这种方法是否因成本问题或与现有的客户端/服务器架构不符而未被广泛采用。
• PeterStuer批评Vanguard反作弊系统在非标准游戏系统上的表现，例如多个自适应同步显示器或安装了Hyper-V、WSL的系统上频繁崩溃。
• a-biad指出反作弊提供商更注重系统的弹性而非保护CDN，并质疑这是否符合Kerchoff's原则。
• bpbp-mango认为Valorant采用的内核级反作弊技术过于侵入用户系统，表达了对这种技术的不满。
• nichochar认为CSGO的反作弊系统在竞争性方面优于其他游戏，但未详细说明原因。

Tracking Anticheat Updates
Posted on
2025-06-26
::
8
Min Read
::
anticheat
security
A few years ago when I was into reverse engineering and binary analysis (and game modding), I did a lot of research into anticheats work. I was curious about tracking their updates, since that would allow me to:
Know when a new version is released
Understand what changes were made
Use older versions for research purposes
So I ended up researching different ways on how to track updates of various anticheats. Some of them are already very well documented, while others haven't been explored much. This post will summarize my findings and outline how they work.
EasyAntiCheat
EasyAntiCheat is widely recognized as one of the most advanced anticheats, and is used in many popular games like Rust, Fortnite, Apex Legends, and more.
Prior to the acquisition by Epic Games, EAC was using their own CDN to distribute updates:
https://download.eac-cdn.com/api/v1/games/{game_id}/client/{system}/download/?uuid=1239688
.
game_id
: unique identifier for each game (e.g. 154 for Apex Legends)
system
: target platform/system (e.g.
wow64_win64
,
mac64
,
linux32_64
).
After the acquisition, they switched to the EpicGames CDN, which has a slightly different URL structure:
https://modules-cdn.eac-prod.on.epicgames.com/modules/{product_id}/{deployment_id}/{system}
. The parameters to this URL are completely different:
product_id
: unique identifier for each game (e.g.
429c2212ad284866aee071454c2125b5
for Rust)
deployment_id
: unique identifier for each deployment (e.g.
76796531e86443548754600511f42e9e
for Rust). This doesn't change when an update is released and is used to identify different game versions.
system
: same as in the old CDN
After downloading the module for a game, we'll have a file which contains data with a very high entropy which is the first indication that it is encrypted or compressed:
$ bat encrypted.bin | ent
Entropy = 7.989390 bits per byte.
Looking at the data, we also can't really identify any patterns or strings. However, across versions the header seems to always stay the same (
a7 ed
): Very interesting 🤔
$ hexyl encrypted.bin | head
┌────────┬─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┬────────┬────────┐

│00000020│ 60 63 66 69 6c 6f 72 75 ┊ 78 7b 7e 81 84 87 8a 8d │`cfiloru┊x{~×××××│

│00000040│ ed 9c 8e d7 80 8c a8 c3 ┊ b1 94 2b fa d2 5c a6 be │××××××××┊××+××\××│
│00000050│ cc 86 86 db dd d5 db d8 ┊ d6 98 91 d5 e3 f3 f7 00 │××××××××┊×××××××⋄│
│00000060│ b4 a5 ed ae be 16 15 c3 ┊ c1 12 cc a5 d7 e9 bd da │×××××••×┊×•××××××│
│00000070│ 2c 26 1f ec 97 79 79 93 ┊ 8c 6b 6e 71 74 77 7a cd │,&•××yy×┊×knqtwz×│

night

data.title: A glob of 99M-year-old amber trapped a zombie fungus erupting from a fly
data.author: jackgavigan
data.article_summary: 科学家在9900万年前的琥珀中发现了一只头部被寄生真菌穿出的苍蝇，以及一只感染类似真菌的年轻蚂蚁。这两种真菌属于已灭绝的Ophiocordyceps属，分别命名为Paleoophiocordyceps gerontoformicae和Paleoophiocordyceps ironomyiae。这类“僵尸真菌”通过操控宿主行为来传播，最终致其死亡。研究表明，这种寄生现象在白垩纪时期已经存在，并可能对当时生态系统产生复杂影响。尽管现代此类真菌主要感染蚂蚁，但苍蝇的案例显示出古代寄生多样性。该发现揭示了寄生真菌进化历史的一角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：琥珀中的真菌及其可能的影响和相关文化联想

不同观点：
• [浪漫化/文化联想的观点] 
   - [davidpfarrell] 认为真菌的主要目的是让昆虫飞入琥珀中，这种表述更像是一种富有想象力的解释。
   - [TruffleLabs] 则直接将真菌从琥珀中提取与电影题材联系起来，暗示这种现象具有潜在的影视创作价值。
   - [nervousvarun] 提到《最后生还者》（The Last of Us）这款游戏，并引用了《Common Side Effects》这本书，以幽默的态度迎接“蘑菇统治者”的到来。

• [文化作品联想的观点]
   - [bluepuma77] 联想到美国编剧David Koepp的喜剧惊悚小说《Cold Storage》，认为这类作品虽然不是他平时阅读的类型，但十分有趣。

• [科学解释与进化论的观点]
   - [pfdietz] 指出这些琥珀中的真菌不一定与今天的Ophiocordyceps真菌相关，强调了真菌对节肢动物的控制是多次独立演化而来的现象，比如影响千足虫的Arthrophaga myriapodina，这种趋同进化在自然界中其实很常见，并以树木的进化为例进行补充说明。

• [历史与进化时间的观点]
   - [downrightmike] 提到真菌的出现可能比恐龙早数亿年，强调了真菌在地球历史中的悠久性。

补充讨论：
• [幽默/调侃]
   - [WediBlino] 和 [usrbinbash] 都以幽默和夸张的方式回应，前者提到“轰炸城市和一切东西”，后者则玩笑道“这就是你想要的僵尸末日”。
   
争议焦点：
• 主要争议点集中在对真菌现象的文化联想与科学解释之间的差异。部分评论者侧重于娱乐和文化联想，而[pfdietz]则强调了科学事实和进化历史，提醒读者不要将不同种类的真菌现象混为一谈。

44391590.article_content:
Fungus can be seen growing out of the head of a fly encased in 99 million-year-old amber.
Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology; Chinese Academy of Sciences/NIGPAS
Sign up for
CNN’s Wonder Theory science newsletter
. Explore the universe with news on fascinating discoveries, scientific advancements and more.
CNN
—
A glob of 99 million-year-old amber has preserved an ancient fly in horror show fashion: with the mushroom-like fruiting body of zombie fungus bursting forth from its head.
The insect, along with a second specimen of a young ant infected with a similar fungus, are two of the oldest examples of a bizarre natural phenomenon that involves fungal parasites hijacking the bodies of their hosts before ultimately killing them.
“Amber gives us this opportunity to visualize the ancient ecological relationships preserved in fossils,” said Yuhui Zhuang, a doctoral student at the Institute of Paleontology at Yunnan University in southwestern China.
“Overall, these two fossils are very rare, at least among the tens of thousands of amber specimens we’ve seen, and only a few have preserved the symbiotic relationship between fungi and insects,” added Zhuang, the lead author of a
study on the fossils p
ublished June 11 in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.
Zhuang and his colleagues named two previously unknown species of ancient fungi of the genus Ophiocordyceps from their research on the amber, which involved using optical microscopes to study the tiny pieces of amber and micro-computed tomography to make 3D images of the fungi-infected insects.
They found the first, named Paleoophiocordyceps gerontoformicae, on the ant and the second, Paleoophiocordyceps ironomyiae, on the fly.
Some Ophiocordyceps species that prey on ant species today are known as
“zombie-ant fungi”
because the fungal parasite can manipulate the behavior of its hosts for its own benefit. The phenomenon inspired the video game behind the HBO TV show
“The Last of Us.”
HBO shares a parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery, with CNN.
“The discovery of these two fossils suggests that terrestrial ecosystems were already very complex, and that Ophiocordyceps, in particular, may have begun to act as “predators” of insects in the Cretaceous period, regulating the populations of certain groups,” Zhuang said via email.
An ant infected with parasitic fungus trapped in 99 million-year-old amber.
Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology, Chinese Academy of Sciences/NIGPAS
Zombie fungi then and now
Today, parasitic fungi, also known as entomopathogenic fungi, infect a wide range of insect groups, including ants, flies, spiders, cicadas and beetles, according to London’s Natural History Museum.
In the case of carpenter ants, the spore of the Ophiocordyceps fungus lands on the head of an ant, enters its brain through a weak area in the insect’s exoskeleton and takes control of the ant to facilitate its spread, said Conrad Labandeira, senior scientist and curator of fossil arthropods at the Smithsonian Museum of Natural History in Washington, DC, who wasn’t involved in the study.
Paleoophiocordyceps likely zombified its hosts in similar ways, according to Labandeira.
“It appears that ants, for some reason, were targeted early for zombification, and currently are the major recipients of this parasitoid fungus,” Labandeira said. He added that flies are only rarely affected by these parasitic fungi today, making a fossilized example particularly interesting.
The species of fungus that infected the prehistoric ant may be an ancestor of zombie-ant fungi, and thus likely controlled its host’s body in similar ways, said study coauthor João Araújo, mycology curator and assistant professor at the Danish Natural History Museum. Very few specimens of ancient parasitic fungi have been discovered, so little is known about their evolution.
The two insects were likely killed by the fungi before getting trapped in the sticky tree resin that ultimately forms amber, said Araújo, noting that most entomopathogenic fungi kill their hosts to produce the fruiting body.
This lost parasite diversity had a significant role in shaping the planet we live on today, said Phil Barden, an associate professor at New Jersey Institute of Technology’s department of biological sciences, who has worked on amber fossils.
“Even as we find a remarkable diversity of organisms entombed in amber, it’s important to remember that we really do only capture the smallest glimpse. For any given fossil ant or beetle, we can imagine all of the parasites, fungus, and bacteria that such insects support,” Barden, who wasn’t involved in the new study, said via email.
A spider that has been killed by an entomopathogenic fungus.
Anton Sorokin/Alamy Stock Photo
It was “fascinating to see some of the strangeness of the natural world that we see today was also present at the height of the age of the dinosaurs,” said study coauthor Edmund Jarzembowski, a professor and associate

data.title: Using DuckDB WASM and Cloudflare R2 to host and query big data (for almost free)
data.author: apwheele
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用DuckDB WASM和Cloudflare R2存储服务以几乎零成本托管和查询大数据。作者Andrew Wheeler描述了通过将150百万行的数据集（约72GB）存储在Cloudflare R2中，并利用DuckDB WASM让用户能够进行即席查询。这种方法避免了传统SQL数据库的高成本，利用静态文件和客户端处理查询，实现了可扩展性和低成本。具体操作包括设置CORS政策、使用自定义域名，以及通过示例代码演示查询过程。整体年成本约为23美元，适用于需要处理大规模数据并向公众提供数据查询服务的场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：R2是否支持"Requester Pays"模式及其在处理大数据集方面的可行性

不同观点：
• [支持"Requester Pays"模式] cedws认为R2应该像S3一样支持"Requester Pays"模式，这样可以避免自己承担公开数据集的费用。他提到过去因为不愿自掏腰包，放弃了一些公开数据的计划。

Using DuckDB WASM + Cloudflare R2 to host and query big data (for almost free)
The motivation here, prompted by a recent question
Abigail Haddad
had on LinkedIn:
For the machines, the context is hosting a dataset of 150 million rows (in another post Abigail stated it was around 72 gigs). And you want the public to be able to make ad-hoc queries on that data. Examples where you may want to do this are public dashboards (think a cities open data site, just puts all the data on R2 and has a front end).
This is the point where traditional SQL databases for websites probably don’t make sense. Databases like
Supabase Postgres
or MySQL can have that much data, given the cost of cloud computing though and what they are typically used for, it does not make much sense to put 72 gigs and use them for data analysis type queries.
Hosting the data as static files though in an online bucket, like
Cloudflare’s R2
, and then querying the data makes more sense for that size. Here to query the data, I also use a
WASM deployed DuckDB
. What this means is I don’t really have to worry about a server at all – it should scale to however many people want to use the service (I am just serving up HTML). The client’s machine handles creating the query and displaying the resulting data via javascript, and Cloudflare basically just pushes data around.
If you want to see it in action, you can check out the
github repo
, or see the
demo deployed on github pages
to illustrate generating queries. To check out a query on my Cloudflare R2 bucket, you can run
SELECT * FROM 'https://data-crimedecoder.com/books.parquet' LIMIT 10;
:
Cloudflare is nice here, since there are no egress charges (big data you need to worry about that). You do get charged for different read/write operations, but the free tiers seem quite generous (I do not know quite how to map these queries to Class B operations in Cloudflare’s parlance, but you get 10 million per month and all my tests only generated a few thousand).
For some notes on this set-up. On Cloudflare, to be able to use DuckDB WASM, I needed to expose the R2 bucket via a custom domain. Using the development url did not work (same
issue as here
). I also set my CORS Policy to:
[
{
"AllowedOrigins": [
"*"
],
"AllowedMethods": [
"GET",
"HEAD"
],
"AllowedHeaders": [
"*"
],
"ExposeHeaders": [],
"MaxAgeSeconds": 3000
}
]
While my Crime De-Coder site is PHP, all the good stuff happens client-side. So you can see some example demo’s of the
GSU book prices data
.
One of the annoying things about this though, with S3 you can partition the files and
query multiple partitions at once
. Here something like
SELECT * FROM read_parquet('https://data-crimedecoder.com/parquet/Semester=*/*') LIMIT 10;
does not work. You can union the partitions together manually. So not sure if there is a way to set up R2 to work the same way as the S3 example (set up a FTP server? let me know in the comments!).
For pricing, for the scenario Abigail had of 72 gigs of data, we then have:
$10 per year for the domain
0.015*72*12 = $13
for storage of the 72 gigs
So we have a total cost to run this of $23 per year. And it can scale to a crazy number of users and very large datasets out of the box. (My usecase here is just $10 for the domain, you get 10 gigs for free.)
Since this can be deployed on a static site, there are free options (like github pages). So the page with the SQL query part is essentially free. (I am not sure if there is a way to double dip on the R2 custom domain, such as just putting the HTML in the bucket.)
While this example only shows generating a table, you can do whatever additional graphics client side. So could make a normal looking dashboard with dropdowns, and those just execute various queries and fill in the graphs/tables.

主要讨论点：利用地衣进行火星地球化

不同观点：
• 支持观点：有评论者认为，利用地衣进行火星地球化是一个可行的初步策略。地衣能够在极端环境下生存，适应性强，可能有助于改变火星大气和土壤环境，为后续的生物和人类生存创造条件。例如，有评论提到地衣可以通过光合作用产生氧气，从而逐步改善火星大气。

• 怀疑观点：另一部分评论者对这一想法持怀疑态度。他们指出，火星的极端温度、高辐射和缺乏液态水等问题，即使是适应力强的地衣也未必能够有效生存和繁殖。例如，有人提到火星上的紫外线辐射对生物体有极大的破坏作用，地衣也可能无法承受。

• 中间立场：还有一些评论者持中间立场，认为地衣或许可以作为火星地球化进程中的一个环节，但不能单靠其完成整个地球化过程。他们建议结合其他科技手段，如人造生态环境和先进的生命支持系统，来辅助地衣发挥作用。有评论提到，可以将地衣与其他微生物或植物联合使用，以提高整体生存率和改造效果。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于地衣在火星极端环境下的生存能力及其对火星大气改造的实际效果。支持者强调其适应性和潜力，怀疑者则关注其实际操作中的困难和限制。

• 有评论讨论了地衣在地球极端环境中的成功案例，如在南极和沙漠中的生存实例，试图以此证明其在火星上的可行性。而反对者则认为火星的环境比地球的极端环境更为严酷，不能简单类比。

• 还有人提出，在考虑利用地衣之前，需要进行更多的实验和研究，包括在地球上的模拟实验和在火星上的实地测试，以评估其真正的潜力和局限性。

data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: **NativeJIT** 是一个开源、跨平台的C++即时编译库，用于高性能编译涉及C数据结构的表达式。该库轻量且快速，仅依赖标准C++运行时，支持Linux、OSX和Windows系统。其生成的代码经过优化，尤其注重寄存器分配。该工具由Bing团队开发，用于Bing搜索引擎中的文档评分过程，根据查询关键词自定义表达式并编译成x64代码，分布式执行。NativeJIT适用于运行时才能确定的表达式，并在大规模查询处理中保证低延迟和高吞吐量。它支持多种算术、逻辑、指针、数组操作及条件语句等。构建NativeJIT需要CMake (2.8.11+) 和现代C++编译器（如gcc 5+、clang 3.4+或VC 2015+）。

主要讨论点：C++表达式、JIT编译器、AST（抽象语法树）的实现和优化，以及不同工具和语言的比较。

不同观点：
• **cout** 认为使用C++表达式创建AST并进行编译很有趣，但建议引入语法糖，例如操作符重载和lambda表达式，以提高可读性和简化控制结构。他提供了ruby-libjit项目的例子来支持其观点，展示如何通过这些改进使JIT编译器的编写更加简单。
   
• **rurban** 提到Bing内部使用了一个更好的版本，但改进尚未合并回GitHub。他引用了BitFunnel/NativeJIT项目的issue来支持这一观点。

• **emmanueloga_** 指出该项目与mathpresso项目相似，提供了一个参考链接。

• **smartaz42** 分享了使用libtcc的经验，强调其API设计出色，尽管生成的代码未经过优化，但编译速度很快。

• **b0a04gl** 关注emit的确定性问题，询问在相同输入情况下是否每次都能得到相同的输出字节，讨论了这一特性对JIT路径记忆化的潜在影响。

• **kookamamie** 质疑为何项目中不使用操作符重载，这与其C++实现相悖，建议通过操作符重载来简化表达式操作。

• **anon-3988** 认为该项目与llvmlite.Builder类似，计划为自己的Python到C到汇编的JIT项目创建类似工具。

• **izabera** 认为示例代码生成不够优化，指出在某些情况下不应设置和拆除堆栈帧，并质疑该工具相对于直接编译和调用动态链接库的优点。

• **nurettin** 半开玩笑地认为这种工作更适合Java，提到了微软的贡献。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个项目的比较和参考链接，如ruby-libjit、mathpresso、libtcc和NativeJIT。
• 对操作符重载和lambda表达式的使用有较多讨论，显示出对代码简洁性和可读性的关注。
• 对emit的确定性和JIT路径记忆化的技术细节有一定探讨，显示出对性能和稳定性的关注。
• 对工具优化能力和相对于传统编译方法的优势也有所争议，显示出对实际应用效果的关注。

NativeJIT
NativeJIT is an open-source cross-platform library for high-performance
just-in-time compilation of expressions involving C data structures.
The compiler is light weight and fast
and it takes no dependencies beyond the standard C++ runtime.
It runs on Linux, OSX, and Windows.
The generated code is optimized with particular attention paid
to register allocation.
The compiler was developed by the
Bing
team for use in the Bing search engine.
One important use is scoring documents containing keywords that match a user's query.
The scoring process attempts to gauge how well each document matches the user's intent,
and as such, depends on the specifics of how each query was phrased.
Bing formulates a custom expression for each query
and then uses NativeJIT to compile the expression into x64 code that will
be run on a large set of candidate documents spread across a cluster of
machines.
We knew from the get go that throughput and latency
would be essential when processing queries at scale,
so we put a lot of effort in to making NativeJIT run fast.
Our design point was scenarios where
The expression isn't known until runtime.
The expression will be evaluated enough times to amortize the cost of compilation.
Latency and throughput demands require low cost for compilation.

• **cout** 认为使用C++表达式创建AST并进行编译很有趣，但建议引入语法糖，例如操作符重载和lambda表达式，以提高可读性和简化控制结构。他提供了ruby-libjit项目的例子来支持其观点，展示如何通过这些改进使JIT编译器的编写更加简单。
   
• **rurban** 提到Bing内部使用了一个更好的版本，但改进尚未合并回GitHub。他引用了BitFunnel/NativeJIT项目的issue来支持这一观点。

• **emmanueloga_** 指出该项目与mathpresso项目相似，提供了一个参考链接。

• **smartaz42** 分享了使用libtcc的经验，强调其API设计出色，尽管生成的代码未经过优化，但编译速度很快。

• **b0a04gl** 关注emit的确定性问题，询问在相同输入情况下是否每次都能得到相同的输出字节，讨论了这一特性对JIT路径记忆化的潜在影响。

• **kookamamie** 质疑为何项目中不使用操作符重载，这与其C++实现相悖，建议通过操作符重载来简化表达式操作。

• **anon-3988** 认为该项目与llvmlite.Builder类似，计划为自己的Python到C到汇编的JIT项目创建类似工具。

• **izabera** 认为示例代码生成不够优化，指出在某些情况下不应设置和拆除堆栈帧，并质疑该工具相对于直接编译和调用动态链接库的优点。

• **nurettin** 半开玩笑地认为这种工作更适合Java，提到了微软的贡献。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个项目的比较和参考链接，如ruby-libjit、mathpresso、libtcc和NativeJIT。
• 对操作符重载和lambda表达式的使用有较多讨论，显示出对代码简洁性和可读性的关注。
• 对emit的确定性和JIT路径记忆化的技术细节有一定探讨，显示出对性能和稳定性的关注。
• 对工具优化能力和相对于传统编译方法的优势也有所争议，显示出对实际应用效果的关注。

data.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了连续血糖监测（CGM）技术的发展及其个人使用体验。作者提到，CGM技术已存在一段时间，主要用于帮助1型糖尿病患者手动调控血糖。虽然过去CGM设备昂贵且需处方，但现在作者能在美国以50美元购买到无需处方的CGM设备，使用寿命为两周。该设备形似厚拨片，每5分钟测量一次血糖，每15分钟传输一次数据。作者使用iPhone接收数据，发现安装过程简单，应用过程略带“赛博朋克”感，但基本无痛。通过该设备，作者发现某些自认健康的饮食其实不利血糖，运动对降血糖效果显著。虽然app不支持数据导出，但可通过Apple Health间接实现。最终，作者认为CGM的游戏化特性有效激励其保持健康血糖水平，并计划未来再次使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：连续血糖监测（CGM）设备的使用体验、效果、准确性、成本以及在非糖尿病人群中的应用。

不同观点：
• [支持CGM的观点]
   - CGM帮助用户重新认识食物与营养，发现一些看似健康的食物（如白面包、芒果干）会导致血糖飙升。[guiambros]
   - 通过CGM监测运动对血糖的影响，发现运动中低血糖问题并调整运动强度，使锻炼更易坚持。[yegle]
   - 推荐使用开源CGM软件Juggluco，认为其功能强大且支持多种设备，尽管界面过时但功能齐全。[yegle]

• [对CGM准确性和成本的质疑]
   - 认为便宜的CGM设备准确性不高，误差范围较大，且多种因素（如时间、压力、睡眠）会影响血糖水平，长期监测需要更昂贵的设备。[bix6]
   - CGM设备价格昂贵，尤其对于动物（如 diabetic cat）而言，性价比不高，停止使用是因为成本问题。[WatchDog]

• [非糖尿病患者的使用体验]
   - 有人认为即使在不食用加工食品的情况下，血糖波动仍无规律，且在举重等运动中血糖会显著升高，而在高强度有氧运动中则会降低。[mondocat]
   - 有人通过CGM结合生酮饮食，成功改善了健康指标（如A1C从7.1降到5.3），强调CGM有助于监控和调整饮食习惯。[cigs645]

• [对CGM长期使用的疑虑]
   - 质疑CGM对非糖尿病患者的长期使用效果，认为这可能是一种健康数据的过度优化，并担心引发健康焦虑（orthorexia）。[ViscountPenguin]
   - 有人对CGM得出的结论感到好奇，尤其想知道哪些被认为健康的食物实际上对血糖不友好。[imjonse]

补充讨论：
• CGM设备的推荐与技术问题
   - 讨论了不同品牌和型号的CGM设备的使用体验，包括对Freestyle Libre系统的推荐和其在不同地区的使用限制问题。[martind81, thor-rodrigues]
   - 提到CGM设备的附件（如过贴）需要提前更换，并推荐了一些实用产品。[utopcell]

争议焦点：
• CGM设备的准确性和性价比：一些人认为便宜的设备不够准确，而昂贵的设备成本过高。
• CGM对非糖尿病患者的实际价值：有人认为CGM有助于健康管理，而另一些人则担心会导致健康数据的过度优化和焦虑。

总的来说，评论中既有对CGM设备带来的健康洞察表示肯定的声音，也有对其成本和准确性的质疑，以及对非糖尿病患者使用CGM的争议。

44418520.article_content:
ImperialViolet
Continuous Glucose Monitoring
(29 Jun 2025)
Continuous glucose monitoring has been a thing for a while. It's a probe that sits just inside your body and measures blood glucose levels frequently. Obviously this is most useful for type 1 diabetics, who need to regulate their blood glucose manually.
(At this point, I would be amiss not to give a nod to the book
Systems Medicine
, which I think most readers would find fascinating. I can't judge whether it's correct or not, but it is a delightful exploration of a bunch of maladies from the perspective of differential equations.)
But CGMs have been both expensive and prescription-only. And I am not a diabetic, type 1 or otherwise. But technology and, more importantly, regulation have apparently marched on, and even in America I
can now buy a CGM
for $50 that lasts for two weeks, over the counter. So CGM technology is now available to the mildly curious, like me.
The device itself looks like a thick guitar pick, and it comes encased inside a much larger lump of plastic that has a pretty serious-looking spring inside. It takes readings every 5 minutes but only transmits every 15 minutes. You need a phone to receive the data and, if the phone is not nearby, it will buffer some number of samples and catch up when it can. The instructions say to keep the phone nearby at all times, so I didn't test how much it will buffer beyond an hour or so.
I've got both an Android and an iPhone, but for this the iPhone was a more convenient device. So everything following probably applies to both ecosystems, but I've only tested it in one.
The app is well made, although you can feel the lawyers & regulators hovering over every part of it. It gives you instructions about how to “install” the sensor, which you do by holding the big lump of plastic with the spring over a suitable spot on your body and then pressing the button.
It's not a
large
needle, but it's not trivial either. There is a soupçon of cyberpunk about applying it to yourself in the bathroom but, honestly, my first thought after pressing the button and hearing the bang of the spring releasing was, “oh, it didn't work.” Because I didn't feel anything at all. But when I lifted the applicator away, there it was. And after a little while it started providing readings.
It's held in place with some sticky plastic, and you can shower with it on. After a week or two the plastic does start to get a bit messed up. Honestly, I would have preferred to have replaced cover every few days, but I only got one in the box.
I placed it on the upper arm as suggested in the instructions. I put it a little bit further around and I didn't have any problems laying down on that side.
What did I learn? In a couple of cases, meals that I thought would be fairly healthy (or at least not terrible) were pretty terrible. There'll be some things that I'll avoid eating more than I had before. In the bucket of “things that should have been obvious but the effect is still stronger than I thought”: exercise really works. Even a brisk walk resets my blood sugar quite significantly. And the
Hawthorne effect
works even when you're doing it to yourself.
The app does not seem to let you export the data. However, at least on iOS you can connect it to Apple Health. And Apple Health does let you export all of your data as a big XML file. So a little bit of Go code later, I have a CSV of everything it recorded and per-day averages and variations.
The sensor will stop working after 15 and a half days. It says exactly 15, but I think it will give you another half day to switch over to another sensor. It comes out easily, although the sticky residue takes some effort to get off the skin.
I did not switch to another sensor. I will probably do it again, but I'll give it a while since, as I expected, most of the insights that I think I'm going to get, I got fairly rapidly. Honestly, I think the gamification of not wanting to spike my blood sugar was perhaps the most effective part of it. I still think it's cool that this is a thing now.

data.title: LLM's Illusion of Alignment
data.author: GodotX
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI对齐（AI alignment）服务及其相关实验的有效性和可信度的讨论

不同观点：
• **helloplanets**：认为AE Studio的网站设计和其声称的AI对齐服务不匹配，怀疑其通过表面工作进行营销，而不是基于实际研究。
• **retsibsi**：承认自己对该领域不熟悉，但质疑实验是否真正证明了当前AI对齐方法（如RLHF）的浅薄，认为实验结果可能只是多维度对齐纠缠的结果。
• **brettkromkamp**：对通过表面约束来改变大规模模型的行为持怀疑态度，认为人类对AI的理解还远远不够。
• **fleebee**：关注网站设计的可访问性问题，特别是动画效果让人感到不适，建议使用减少动效的媒体查询。
• **skybrian**：认为实验结果与之前讨论的“ emergent alignment”论文结果相似，但对网站声称的不同主张表示疑问。
• **Dilettante_**：引用实验描述并以幽默方式表达对编程能力与人格特质相关的刻板印象，实际上是在调侃实验结论。
• **pastapliiats**：认为网站导航困难，且LLM的回应分类可能有问题，质疑数据的充分性和分类准确性。
• **andai**：提到一个相关研究，特别是后续实验显示模型在触发词出现前表现正常，触发词后表现出恶意输出，认为这更令人担忧。
• **j16sdiz**：批评网站设计糟糕，难以阅读GPT-4o的引用内容。
• **rooftopzen**：认为实验结果是预期行为，指出微调会改变权重，安全约束会变弱，且模型对某些群体的回应反映了训练数据中的偏见。
• **cwegener**：寻找更详细的论文或文章，因为网站设计使其难以获取信息。
• **barrenko**：引用LessWrong上的一篇文章，暗示其与当前讨论相关。
• **jdefr89**：认为LLM的输出是其训练方式的产物，本质上只是一个神经网络，没有真正的理解能力。
• **nurettin**：提到之前的审查事件，暗示对当前讨论有类似感受。

补充讨论：
- 网站设计问题：多位评论者（fleebee, j16sdiz, cwegener）提到网站设计难以使用，影响了对内容的访问和理解。
- 实验设计和数据问题：pastapliiats和retsibsi对实验数据和结论的有效性提出质疑，认为数据量不足和分类可能有误。
- AI对齐方法的浅薄性：brettkromkamp和retsibsi对当前AI对齐方法的有效性表示怀疑，认为这些方法可能只是表面工作。
- 模型行为的可预测性：rooftopzen和jdefr89指出模型行为是其训练数据和微调结果的反映，强调了对模型行为的现实期望。

data.title: Ultrasound toothbrush promises painless checks for hidden gum problems
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种牙刷形状的超声波换能器，用于无创检测牙龈疾病。传统的牙周探查方法 uncomfortable 且可能遗漏早期症状，而这种新型设备通过高频超声波能够生成高质量的牙齿和牙龈图像，尤其适用于后牙等难以触及的部位。在对猪牙齿的实验中，该设备的测量结果与传统手工探查结果相近，证明了其可靠性。该技术有望实现无痛、精准的牙龈健康检查，帮助早期诊断和治疗。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电动牙刷及牙科领域创新的接受度和市场化

不同观点：
• sinoue：对创新的积极态度，联想到《质量效应》牙刷，表现出对新产品的好奇和期待。
• wjnc：对牙科行业创新的悲观看法，认为由于私募股权的控制，创新往往被压制。牙科行业更关注利润，而非患者的健康结果。例举了牙医操作时间和计费方式的问题，并暗示供应链控制可能是市场垄断的一种手段。
• eminemence：提供了一种氟化物的替代品，引用了科学研究，展示了一种有助于牙齿恢复的创新产品，表现出对实际健康创新的关注。

by
American Chemical Society
edited by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes

and

The toothbrush-shaped ultrasound transducer (left image) features a small head size (right image), allowing easy access to premolars and molars in the back of the mouth. Credit: Adapted from ACS Sensors 2025, DOI: 10.1021/acssensors.5c00521
When visiting the dentist, you might remember being poked and prodded by a thin metal instrument to check your teeth and gums. This technique, called periodontal probing, is used to look for signs of gum disease. Now, researchers publishing in
ACS Sensors
report a toothbrush-shaped ultrasound transducer that can provide a less invasive screening for gum disease. In proof-of-concept demonstrations on animal tissues, the device produced measurements similar to those of a manual probe.
Gum disease is a common condition affecting tissue that surrounds and supports teeth. If left untreated, it causes the gums to pull away from the teeth, creating pockets where harmful bacteria can grow. Currently, manual periodontal probing is the standard way to check for
gum disease
, but the technique is uncomfortable and can miss early stages. So, Jesse Jokerst and colleagues developed a small, noninvasive ultrasound method capable of imaging teeth and gums—even hard-to-reach molars and premolars at the back of the mouth.
Ultrasounds work by sending sound waves into the body. When the sound waves encounter a structure, like gum tissue or a tooth, they are reflected and detected by a transducer. The transducer then converts the reflected
sound waves
into an image. Currently, most
ultrasound transducers
have large heads that are about the same size as a wireless earbuds case. Although they work for larger parts of the body, these transducers cannot access smaller spaces like those in the mouth. Smaller transducers that are about half the length and width of traditional devices are available, but
current models
have limited image resolution because they are only able to produce and detect low frequencies. To overcome these limitations, the researchers created an even smaller toothbrush-shaped transducer that operates at a higher frequency and can produce high-quality images of teeth and gums.
To test the transducer's accuracy, the researchers used the new instrument to measure the gum thickness and gum height of pig
teeth
. Then the researchers repeated the measurements using a manual metal periodontal probe. After analyzing the correlation between the two sets of measurements, the team found that the
ultrasound
measurements were statistically similar to those of the manual technique. The results support the reliability of the toothbrush-shaped transducer as a less invasive technique for monitoring gum health.
"We designed this tool to meet the realities of clinical dentistry—it is miniaturized, accurate and easy to use. Future work will use this device with patients to image below the gumline, where we will monitor treatments and diagnose earlier to reduce dental pain and help patients keep a healthy smile," says Jokerst.
More information:
Suhel Khan et al, Performance Evaluation of a Miniaturized, Toothbrush-Shaped Ultrasound Transducer for Periodontal Imaging,
ACS Sensors
(2025).

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何在Linux环境下进行Windows程序的交叉编译和开发，具体包括以下内容：

1. **交叉编译C代码**：使用mingw-w64工具链编译Windows可执行文件。
2. **链接DLL**：演示如何编译并使用Raylib的DLL文件。
3. **安装SBCL**：通过Wine在Linux上安装Windows版的SBCL，并配置使其在Emacs中作为REPL运行。
4. **加载DLL文件**：在Lisp环境中加载Windows DLL。
5. **构建可执行文件**：将Lisp程序编译为Windows的.exe可执行文件。
6. **路径处理**：讨论Linux和Windows下路径的差异，并介绍处理路径的便利工具。
7. **在Emacs中使用Wine-based SBCL**：通过配置SLY或Slime，在Emacs中使用通过Wine运行的SBCL。

通过这些步骤，开发者可以在Linux环境下顺利开发和测试Windows应用程序。

不同观点：

争议焦点：
• 什么是真正的跨编译。 [aidenn0] 认为使用Wine并不算真正的跨编译，而[haunter] 则提出了Cosmopolitan作为另一种跨编译方案。这反映了在跨平台开发中对“跨编译”定义的不同理解和实践方法的分歧。

44401358.article_content:
Table of Contents
Cross-compiling C
Linking to a DLL
Installing SBCL
Pathnames
Wine-based SBCL in Emacs
Loading Windows DLLs
Building Executables
Cross-compiling Common Lisp for Windows
By Colin on 2025-06-28
I recently enabled Windows support for my
Raylib
bindings library and a game of mine that uses it,
Aero Fighter
. The process was surprisingly smooth.
This article describes how to:
cross-compile C code for Windows from Linux
install a Windows-based SBCL with
Wine
run that SBCL as your REPL in Linux-based Emacs
load
.dll
files into a Lisp image
produce a
.exe
executable of a Lisp program
Cross-compiling C
We can easily produce Windows executables from Linux with no extra configuration just by using the correct compiler toolchain. On Arch Linux:
pacman -S mingw-w64-toolchain
Then, given the following C code:
#include
<stdio.h>
int
main
()
{
printf
(
"Hello, World!
\n
"
);
return
0
;
}
we can compile and run it like so:
> x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc hello.c
> wine ./a.exe
Hello, World!
Linking to a DLL
Feel free to skip this if you not interested in linking to C code.
Assuming you have a local clone of Raylib, it can be cross-compiled by setting the following within its
src/Makefile
:
RAYLIB_LIBTYPE   ?= SHARED
HOST_PLATFORM_OS ?= LINUX
PLATFORM_OS      ?= WINDOWS
CC = x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc
AR = x86_64-w64-mingw32-ar
Then a call to
make PLATFORM_OS=WINDOWS
will produce a
.dll
file. Now, given this sample C:
#include
"raylib.h"
int
main
(
void
)
{
const
int
screenWidth
=
800
;
const
int
screenHeight
=
450
;
InitWindow
(
screenWidth
,
screenHeight
,
"raylib example 01 - Windows"
);
SetTargetFPS
(
60
);
while
(!
WindowShouldClose
())
{
BeginDrawing
();
ClearBackground
(
RAYWHITE
);
DrawText
(
"Saluete!"
,
190
,
200
,
20
,
LIGHTGRAY
);
EndDrawing
();
}
CloseWindow
();
return
0
;
}
Copy (or symlink)
raylib.h
,
raylib.dll
, and
libraylibdll.a
to the same directory, and compile it with:
> x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc hello.c -L"." -lraylib
Then,
wine ./a.exe
should open a Raylib window. Quit with
ESC
.
Installing SBCL
Visit the
SBCL Downloads
page and download the
.msi
installer file by clicking on the Windows cell of the Binaries matrix. Run
wine
on this. By default the
sbcl.exe
binary is installed to:
$HOME/.wine/drive_c/Program Files/Steel Bank Common Lisp/
You can confirm its function by running:
wine $HOME/.wine/drive_c/Program Files/Steel Bank Common Lisp/sbcl.exe
Try inspecting the content of the
*features*
list:
(:ARENA-ALLOCATOR :X86-64 :GENCGC :64-BIT :ANSI-CL :COMMON-LISP
:IEEE-FLOATING-POINT :LITTLE-ENDIAN :PACKAGE-LOCAL-NICKNAMES :SB-LDB
:SB-PACKAGE-LOCKS :SB-SAFEPOINT :SB-THREAD :SB-UNICODE :SBCL :WIN32)
Notice the presence of
:WIN32
and the lack of
:LINUX
and
:UNIX
. It's Windows!
Pathnames
Feel free to ignore this section, it is optional information.
Filepaths work differently between Linux and Windows, and we can observe how SBCL handles this. In our REPL:
> (inspect #p"Z:/home/colin/code/foo.json")
The object is a PATHNAME.
0. NAMESTRING: NIL
1. HOST: #<SB-IMPL::WIN32-HOST {1100039A13}>
2. DEVICE: "Z"
3. DIR+HASH: ((:ABSOLUTE "home" "colin" "code") . 3675096247244793922)
4. NAME: "foo"
5. TYPE: "json"
6. VERSION: :NEWEST
Notice that the
:device
field is actually populated. On Linux this would have been
nil
. Notice also that, for our convenience, the path component separator is
/
and not those accursed backslashes!
The
filepaths
library offers additional convenience regarding paths, and supports both Linux and Windows.
Wine-based SBCL in Emacs
vend
is a dependency manager for Common Lisp, and luckily it helps us simplify our Windows setup, since we don't need to bother with a Quicklisp installation within Wine. Since
vend repl
allows us to run any compiler and load our systems with all of our project dependencies available, why not just ask it to run SBCL through Wine as above?
> pwd
/home/colin/code/common-lisp/filepaths
> vend repl wine /home/colin/.wine/drive_c/Program\ Files/Steel\ Bank\ Common\ Lisp/sbcl.exe
> (asdf:test-system :filepaths)
;; ... compiling, etc. ...
Passed:    79
Failed:     0
Skipped:    0
Likewise,
vend test
"just works":
> vend test wine /home/colin/.wine/drive_c/Program\ Files/Steel\ Bank\ Common\ Lisp/sbcl.exe
[vend] Running tests.
;; ... yeah yeah ...
Passed:    79
Failed:     0
Skipped:    0
It's able to find all of our vendored dependencies by virtue of the fact that our Linux filesystem is also available through Wine under
Z:
. When
vend
internally asks
uiop
where we currently are, we get what we'd expect:
> (uiop:getcwd)
#P"Z:/home/colin/code/common-lisp/filepaths/"
Now that we've proven we can load systems through Wine, we can configure
Sly
to use our Wine-based SBCL as an in-editor REPL:
(setq sly-lisp-implementations
'((sbcl ("vend" "repl" "sbcl" "--dynamic-space-size" "4GB"))
;; ... other compilers ...
(wine ("vend" "repl" "wine" "/home/colin/.wine/drive_c/Program Files/Steel Bank Common Lisp/sbcl.exe"))))
Adjust as necessary for
Slime
. Then,
SPC m ;
in Doom (or
C-u

data.title: LetsEncrypt – Expiration Notification Service Has Ended
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: Let's Encrypt已于2025年6月4日停止发送证书到期通知邮件。该决定基于以下原因：越来越多用户已实现证书续期的自动化，继续发送通知需保留大量电子邮件地址，有隐私风险，且该服务每年花费数万美元，资金可用于其他基础设施建设。此外，通知系统增加了技术复杂性。建议用户使用第三方服务如Red Sift Certificates Lite获取到期通知。Let's Encrypt已删除存储的与证书颁发相关的电子邮件地址，未来通过ACME API提供的邮件地址将转至ISRG的邮件列表系统，用户可自行选择订阅相关更新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Let’s Encrypt 取消证书过期通知邮件的决定及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• 支持取消通知：
  - [scrapheap]: 用户不应依赖证书颁发机构（CA）来提醒证书过期，而应自行设置监控机制。
  - [builtsimple]: 取消通知是明智之举，依赖邮件提醒是自动化实践不佳的表现。通过Prometheus和cert-manager等工具可以实现更好的监控。
  - [jgaa]: 自行编写工具来验证证书状态，不依赖第三方通知。
  - [Jazgot]: 此举促使其实现证书自动更新，认为这是更好的实践。

• 反对或担忧取消通知：
  - [weird-eye-issue]: 建议Let’s Encrypt与Postmark等公司合作，通过提及赞助商获得免费邮件服务。

44419496.article_content:
Blog
Expiration Notification Service Has Ended
By Josh Aas ·
June 26, 2025
Since its inception, Let’s Encrypt has been sending expiration notification emails to subscribers that have provided an email address to us via the ACME API. This service ended on June 4, 2025. The decision to end the service is the result of the following factors:
Over the past 10 years more and more of our subscribers have been able to put reliable automation into place for certificate renewal.
Providing expiration notification emails means that we have to retain millions of email addresses connected to issuance records. As an organization that values privacy, removing this requirement is important to us.
Providing expiration notifications costs Let’s Encrypt tens of thousands of dollars per year, money that we believe can be better spent on other aspects of our infrastructure.
Providing expiration notifications adds complexity to our infrastructure, which takes time and attention to manage and increases the likelihood of mistakes being made. Over the long term, particularly as we add support for new service components, we need to manage overall complexity by phasing out system components that can no longer be justified.
For those who would like to continue receiving expiration notifications, we recommend using a third party service such as
Red Sift Certificates Lite
(formerly Hardenize). Red Sift’s monitoring service providing expiration emails is free of charge for up to 250 certificates. More monitoring options can be found
here
.
We have deleted the email addresses provided to Let’s Encrypt via the ACME API that were stored in our CA database in association with issuance data. This doesn’t affect addresses signed up to mailing lists and other systems. They are managed in a separate ISRG system unassociated with issuance data.
Going forward, if an email address is provided to Let’s Encrypt via the ACME API, Let’s Encrypt will not store the address but will instead forward it to the general ISRG mailing list system unassociated with any account data. If the email address has not been seen before, that system may send an onboarding email with information about how to subscribe to various sources of updates.
If you’d like to stay informed about technical updates and other news about Let’s Encrypt and our parent nonprofit,
ISRG
, based on the preferences you choose, you can sign up for our email lists below:

data.title: Want to meet people, try charging them for it?
data.author: ArneVogel
data.article_summary: 自2017年以来，作者一直坚持写博客，并希望通过公开演讲与志同道合的人建立联系。尽管博客和推特获得了超过100万次浏览和2万名粉丝，但很少有人主动联系他。然而，从去年11月开始，他尝试向每场聊天收费100美元，费用捐给教育非营利组织，结果立刻见到了成效。人们积极响应，捐款后与他讨论各种话题，如数据库趋势、编程成功秘诀、开发者营销等。迄今为止，他已为教育非营利组织筹集了近6000美元。尽管收费让他不再能免费帮助那些最需要帮助的人，但他通过30岁生日时的一次特别活动部分缓解了这个问题。作者认为，这种模式让他能轻松持续地做出贡献，同时也结识了许多有趣的人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该对咨询服务收费，以及收费对互动性质的影响

不同观点：
• rpastuszak认为自己通过Say Hi页面与200多人交流，其中许多人建议他应对通话收费。他的通话常涉及技术/产品建议，许多询问者已有丰富经验并愿意付费。然而，他担心收费会减少与经济困难者或有趣的陌生人之间的偶然互动。他还提到自己享受这种交流，并从中学到很多，因此在考虑是否收费。

• wodenokoto提到一个类似实验：在“免费拥抱”旁边设立“收费拥抱”，结果收费拥抱收集到更多回应。这表明收费可能改变人们的反应。

• BlackFly指出，即使提供免费咨询，也很少有人询问。他认为收费能创造预期，促使人们更愿意询问，因为付费意味着更有可能得到回应。

• jpalomaki引用《魔鬼经济学》中的例子，说明收费可能使某些行为变得更 socially acceptable，例如迟到的罚款反而增加了迟到现象。

• poisonborz认为作者已有名气并为慈善收费，这与普通人情况不同。

• Almondsetat不认为有名气和可达邮箱却不被联系是常见现象。

• ericmcer分享了自己付费咨询的经历，认为付费能创造一种无需顾虑的交流环境，且在生活中有价值。

• 11235813213455提到自己尝试通过收费筛选真正感兴趣的购房者。

• thenthenthen描述了自己参与小型收费聊天活动的积极体验，尽管自己并不出名。

• mmarian提到自己博客虽然有联系方式但没人联系，尽管有人提到读过博客。

• Unit327将这种行为与图书馆罚款或托儿迟到罚款相比较，指出从社会义务向财务交易的转变。

• landgenoot指出博客和易联系情况下，多数人只问具体问题而非出于兴趣。

• KolibriFly认为将隐性社会成本显性化有解放作用，给双方明确的结构。

• daedrdev认为成功收费表明专业性足够得到他人付费。

• lewantmontreal提到LLMs前希望有付费问答平台，以确保获得特定信息。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于收费是否会改变交流的本质以及是否会影响与有趣陌生人的互动。
- 收费可能创造预期和信任，但也可能排除某些群体。
- 个人享受和学习价值也是是否收费的重要考虑因素。
- 有名气和为慈善收费的情况下，收费的合理性可能不同。

44419986.article_content:
I have been blogging consistently since 2017. And one of my goals in
speaking publicly was always to connect with like-minded people. I
always left my email and hoped people would get in touch. Even while
my blog and twitter became popular, passing 1M views and 20k
followers, I basically never had people get in touch to chat or meet up.
So it felt kind of ridiculous when last November I
started charging
people $100 to chat
. I mean, who am
I? But people started showing up fairly immediately. Now granted the
money did not go to me. It went to an education non-profit and I
merely received the receipt.
And at this point I've met a number of interesting people, from VCs to
business professors to undergraduate students to founders and everyone
in between. People wanting to talk about trends in databases, about
how to succeed as a programmer, about marketing for developers, and so
on. Women and men thoughout North America, Europe, Africa, New
Zealand, India, Nepal, and so on. And I've raised nearly $6000 for
educational non-profits.
How is it that you go from giving away your time for free and getting
no hits to charging and almost immediately getting results? For one,
every person responded very positively to it being a fundraiser. It
also helps me be entirely shameless about sharing on social media
every single time someone donates; because it's such a positive thing.
But also I think that in "charging" for my time it helps people feel
more comfortable about actually taking my time, especially when we
have never met. It gives you a reasonable excuse to take time from
an internet rando.
On the other hand, a lot of people come for advice and I think giving
advice is pretty dangerous, especially since my background is not
super conventional. I try to always frame things as just sharing my
opinion and my perspective and that they should talk with many others
and not take my suggestions without consideration.
And there's also the problem that by charging everyone for my time
now, I'm no longer available to people who could maybe use it the
most. I do mention on my page that I will still take calls from people
who don't donate, as my schedule allows. But to be honest I feel less
incentivized to spend time when people do not donate. So I guess this
is an issue with the program.
But I mitigated even this slightly, and significantly jump-started the
program, during
my 30th birthday
when
I took calls with any person who donated at least $30.
Anyway, I picked this path because I have wanted to get involved with
helping students figure out their lives and careers. But without a
degree I am literally unqualified for many volunteering programs. And
I always found the time commitments for non-profits painful.
So until starting this I figured it wouldn't be until I retire that I
find some way to make a difference. But ultimately I kept meeting
people who were starting their own non-profits now or donated
significantly to help students. Peer pressure. I wanted to do my part
now. And 30 minutes of my time in return for a donation receipt has
been an easy trade.
While only raising a humble $6,000 to date, the
Chat for
Education
program has been more
successful than I imagined. I've met many amazing people through
it. And it's something that should be easy to keep up indefinitely.
I hope to meet you through it too!
I wrote about trying to meet like-minded people and fundraising for educational non-profits.

data.title: Thousands in Norway told they had won life-changing sums in lottery error
data.author: zqna
data.article_summary: 挪威国有博彩公司Norsk Tipping因欧元兑挪威克朗的转换错误，误向数千客户通知他们赢得巨额奖金。错误导致公司CEO引咎辞职，并引发客户、监管机构及挪威文化大臣的强烈批评。虽然公司迅速修正了错误信息，并确认未进行错误支付，但事件已在客户中造成混乱，一些人在发现错误前已开始庆祝。该公司承认过去一年存在多次技术问题，并表示将继续调查此次事件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于系统中一个明显错误的讨论，特别是该错误是否能通过自动化测试避免，以及对错误后果的看法。

不同观点：
• [mailund] 认为这种明显的数学错误（数值被乘以100而不是除以100）应该通过基本的自动化测试立即发现。这暗示了系统可能缺乏足够的自动化测试覆盖，从而引发了对测试流程的质疑。

• [Neywiny] 试图澄清错误的实际影响，提出这个错误可能意味着某人预期得到x欧元，但实际上他们得到了(x/100)/100欧元，经过两次错误计算。这表明对错误的具体影响存在一定的困惑，并尝试解释错误是如何发生的。

• [jagermo] 没有直接参与错误本身的讨论，而是通过分享一个幽默视频（Reno 911 clip）来调侃或缓解讨论的紧张气氛，暗示这种错误可能在实际操作中带来荒谬的结果。

• [gsky] 用一句简短的讽刺评论“Test failures for the greater good”回应，可能是在暗示有时候测试失败反而被忽略或认为有其他更大的好处，表现出对测试失败的某种无奈或接受态度。

• [Double_a_92] 质疑了因开发人员的打字错误（typo）导致CEO离职的合理性，认为一个战术上的错误不应该直接影响公司的战略决策，暗示对错误后果的处理方式存在争议。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于这个错误是否真的如[mailund]所说，可以通过自动化测试轻易避免，还是如[gsky]所暗示的那样，有时测试失败可能被容忍。
• [Double_a_92] 提出了对错误后果的质疑，特别是CEO离职是否与这个错误直接相关，这引发了对公司管理层反应的讨论。
• [Neywiny] 的澄清尝试表明，对于错误的具体计算方式和影响仍存在一定的不确定性，可能需要进一步的技术解释。

The error has triggered sharp criticism from customers, regulators and the Norwegian minister of culture.
Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
The error has triggered sharp criticism from customers, regulators and the Norwegian minister of culture.
Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty Images
Norway
Thousands in Norway told they had won life-changing sums in lottery error
Calculation mistake by state-owned gambling operator, Norsk Tipping, prompts CEO to resign
Caolán Magee
Sun 29 Jun 2025 15.56 EDT
Last modified on Mon 30 Jun 2025 03.10 EDT
Share
Thousands of Norwegians were mistakenly told they had won life-changing sums in the country’s Eurojackpot draw after an error by the state-owned gambling operator, Norsk Tipping.
In a statement on Friday, Norsk Tipping said “several thousand customers were notified of incorrectly high prizes”. The mistake has prompted the resignation of the company’s chief executive.
The company receives prize amounts from Germany in euros, which are then converted to Norwegian kroner.
“It is during this conversion that a manual error has been made in the code that is entered into our game engine,” the company said in a statement. “The amount has been multiplied by 100, instead of being divided by 100.”
The inflated sums were displayed on the company’s website and mobile app on Friday but were later removed. Norsk Tipping confirmed no incorrect payouts were made.
The error has triggered sharp criticism from customers, regulators and the Norwegian minister of culture. The company held an emergency meeting with the ministry of culture on Saturday to explain the incident.
On Sunday, CEO Tonje Sagstuen announced she would step down from the role she had held since September 2023. “As a manager, it has been my responsibility to handle the mistakes that have occurred,” she said in a statement.
“Therefore, it is also incredibly sad to leave Norsk Tipping and all the talented people who work in Hamar. I will miss everyone I have worked with, but I am confident that all the improvement processes we have initiated are in good hands.”
Several Norwegians told NRK they had begun celebrating before discovering the mistake.

data.title: New proof dramatically compresses space needed for computation
data.author: baruchel
data.article_summary: 计算机科学家Ryan Williams在ACM计算理论研讨会上提出了一项突破性发现，颠覆了近50年的假设。传统观点认为，解决一个问题所需的时间步数（t）与其所需的内存 bits 数大致相等。然而，Williams 证明，任何在 t 步内可解决的问题其实只需约 √t bits 的内存。例如，一个100步的计算可能只需约10 bits。这一发现通过“归约”实现，将一个问题转化为另一个数学等价的问题，从而有效重用内存空间。这一进展表明，计算效率的真正限制不在于内存大小，而在于如何智慧地使用它。这一发现被认为是一次“极其意外”的突破，对计算复杂性理论具有重大影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ryan Williams关于计算时间与内存需求关系的新发现及其理论和实际应用

不同观点：
• [zerof1l] 介绍Ryan Williams的发现：传统观点认为计算时间t步需要t bits的内存，但Williams发现只需要大约sqrt(t) bits，即100步计算只需约10 bits。这个发现挑战了传统认知。
• [cyrillite] 推荐一个详细解释该理论的YouTube视频，强调科学传播的重要性。
• [JohnKemeny] 引用相关讨论，指出算法中内存比时间更为重要，并提供其他讨论链接。
• [mikewarot] 对逆向问题感兴趣，即通过增加内存来减少时间，并提到使用记忆化（Memoization）可能是最好的方法。同时，提到停机问题，暗示逆向操作可能不可行。
• [utopcell] 指出Williams的结果仅适用于 oblivious 算法（步骤i不依赖于步骤j < i的决策），而大多数实际算法是非 oblivious的。认为该结果对实际应用影响有限，但仍是一项重要的理论进展。

补充讨论：
• [gwbas1c] 提到实际编程中的代码效率问题，认为通过提高编程技能可以更好地利用现有硬件，并提出AI可能的帮助。
• [krackers] 和 [JohnKemeny] 类似，提供相关讨论链接。
• [gweinberg] 对理论表示不理解，质疑为何循环n次的计算需要增加内存。
• [kristianp] 认为该理论非常理论化，质疑其对实际算法的意义。
• [baruchel] 提供无付费墙的链接，方便他人访问相关论文。
• [bluenose69] 引用SciAm文章中的一句话，对log(t)的解释感到困惑。
• [snickerbockers] 反驳 [bluenose69] 的困惑，指出其对有理数理解的错误。

争议焦点：
• 该理论结果的实际应用价值：一些评论者质疑该理论发现对实际算法的意义，认为其仅适用于特定类型的算法（oblivious 算法），对大多数实际算法影响有限。
• 对理论细节的理解和解释：部分评论者对理论中的数学概念（如log(t)）及其解释感到困惑，并出现不同意见的争论。

总结：评论围绕Ryan Williams的计算时间与内存关系的新发现展开，主要讨论了该理论的适用范围、实际应用价值以及对数学概念的理解争议。

New Proof Dramatically Compresses Space Needed for Computation
Surprising new work bucks 50 years of assumptions about the trade-offs between computation space and time
By
Max Springer
edited by
Sarah Lewin Frasier
Thomas Fuchs
Join Our Community of Science Lovers!
Sign Up for Our Free Daily Newsletter
Enter your email
I agree my information will be processed in accordance with the Scientific American and Springer Nature Limited
Privacy Policy
.
Sign Up
Once upon a time computers filled entire rooms, reading numbers from spinning tapes and churning them through wires to do chains of basic arithmetic. Today they slip into our pockets, performing in a tiny fraction of a second what used to take hours. But
even as chips shrink and gain speed
, theorists are flipping the question from how much computation space we can pack into a machine to how little is enough to get the job done.
This inquiry lies at the heart of computational complexity, a measure of the limits of what problems can be solved and at what cost in time and space. For nearly 50 years theorists believed that if solving a problem takes
t
steps, it should also need roughly
t
bits of memory—the 0s and 1s that a machine uses to record information. (Technically, that equation was
t/
log(
t
), but for the numbers involved log(
t
) is typically negligibly small.) If a task involves 100 steps, for instance, you’d expect to need at least 100 bits, enough to diligently log each step. Using fewer bits was thought to require more steps—like alphabetizing your books by swapping them one by one on the shelf instead of pulling them all out and reshelving them. But in a
surprising finding
described this week at the ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing in Prague, Massachusetts Institute of Technology computer scientist Ryan Williams found that any problem solvable in time
t
needs only about √
t
bits of memory: a 100-step computation could be compressed and solved with something on the order of 10 bits. “This result shows the prior intuition is completely false,” Williams says. “I thought there must be something wrong [with the proof] because this is
extremely
unexpected.”
The breakthrough relies on a “reduction,” a means of transforming one problem into another that may seem unrelated but is mathematically equivalent. With reductions, packing a suitcase maps onto determining a monthly budget: the size of your suitcase represents your total budget, pieces of clothing correspond to potential expenses, and carefully deciding which clothes can fit is like allocating your budget. Solving one problem would then directly solve the other. This idea is at the core of Williams’s result: any problem can be transformed into one you can solve by cleverly reusing space, deftly cramming the necessary information into just a square-root number of bits. Thus, the original problem must be solvable with this compact container.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
“This progress is unbelievable,” says Mahdi Cheraghchi, a computer scientist at the University of Michigan. “Before this result, there were problems you could solve in a certain amount of time, but many thought you couldn’t do so with such little space.” Williams’s finding, he adds, is “a step in the right direction that we didn’t know how to take.”
While computers have continued to shrink, our theoretical understanding of their efficiency has exploded, suggesting that the real constraint is not how much memory we have but how wisely we use it.

data.title: The Plot of the Phantom, a text adventure that took 40 years to finish
data.author: SeenNotHeard
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者历经40年终于完成了自己青少年时期开始制作的文字冒险游戏《The Plot of the Phantom》。作者在1984年受Infocom文字冒险游戏系列启发，开始在Atari 800电脑上用BASIC编程制作该游戏，但由于技术限制和个人兴趣转移，游戏一度被搁置。2018年，作者了解到Inform 7这一现代编程语言可以用于制作文字冒险游戏，并在疫情期间利用空闲时间重新拾起这个项目，最终完成了游戏。新版游戏在保留原始地图和谜题的基础上进行了修改，减少了暴力元素，并加入了一些自传性内容。现在，玩家可以在浏览器中体验这款游戏，虽然流程较短且难度不高，但对怀旧玩家而言仍具吸引力。作者对完成这一长期项目感到既高兴又感慨。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文本冒险游戏的开发、历史、技术演进以及可能的创新应用

不同观点：
• vunderba 认为可以通过增加动词同义词来使解析器更灵活，并分享了自己在开发过程中因过度复杂化游戏本体而导致游戏将角色放入 inventory 的趣事。
• Nevermark 分享了自己从早期接触文本冒险游戏到后来开发复杂游戏的经历，强调了在编程和创新方面的学习经验，并对某些老游戏的遗忘表示遗憾。
• ThinkingGuy 提到在1980年代，自制文本冒险游戏是常见项目，并表示自己存档了一些未完成或未分享的游戏。
• Pet_Ant 提到了一个来自东欧的仍在开发的冒险游戏，该游戏具有复杂的因果关系和深度，但无法找到该游戏的具体信息。
• amiga386 推荐了一本关于冒险游戏编程的书，鼓励大家学习冒险游戏编程的秘诀。
• noisy_boy 和 janeway 对游戏的幽默和趣味性表示赞赏。
• matthewsinclair 分享了自己在不同硬件平台上完成游戏开发的经历。
• BryanLegend 以幽默方式提到是否是George RR Martin编写了该游戏。
• alienbaby 分享了自己使用PAWS在Amstrad PCW上开发文本冒险游戏的经历，并考虑重新挖掘出来。
• scoot 提出文本冒险游戏在第二语言学习中的应用可能性，并讨论了LLM（大型语言模型）在改善用户体验方面的潜力，认为LLM应作为理解玩家指令的翻译器而非游戏状态的仲裁者。
• ninetyninenine 进一步阐述了LLM在文本冒险游戏中的应用，认为LLM可以作为游戏状态与玩家之间的接口，保持游戏世界的一致性和结构，同时增加动态性。

补充讨论：
• 关于LLM在文本冒险游戏中的应用存在一定讨论，scoot 和 ninetyninenine 都认为LLM可以改善游戏体验，但在LLM的具体功能和角色上存在细微差别。scoot 认为LLM应仅作为翻译器，而 ninetyninenine 则建议LLM作为游戏状态的动态报告者。
• 对老游戏的遗忘和保存问题被提及，Nevermark 对 Mystery Mansion 等游戏的遗忘表示遗憾，而 ThinkingGuy 提到许多未共享的游戏可能存在于旧软盘中。
• Pet_Ant 提到的东欧冒险游戏引发了对特定深度和因果关系复杂的游戏的兴趣，但具体游戏信息不详。

争议焦点：
• LLM在文本冒险游戏中的具体应用和角色是讨论中的一个潜在争议点，虽然都认可LLM的潜力，但在其具体功能上存在不同看法。

44398809.article_content:
Blog
Posted June 23, 2025.
You can now play "The Plot of the Phantom," the text adventure game that took me 40 years to finish
tl;dr: I finished writing a text adventure game I started when I was a teenager, and you can
play it in a browser right now
.
If you knew me in 1984, you would also know that you could find me
glued to a chair in front of our family's Atari 800 personal computer
, typing out BASIC programs from issues of COMPUTE! magazine and letting the summer days go by. I was also obsessed with the
Infocom series of text adventure games
, although I'd have to go to a friend's house to play them because they were almost exclusively for the Commodore 64.
So
of course
I set out to make my own text adventure game!
The Plot of the Phantom
was a Zork-alike dungeon crawl with plenty of hide-and-seek puzzle quests for objects required to advance the game (e.g. to open a door, you needed to find the key, which was in the bucket at the bottom of the well, but you needed to find a rope first, etc.). I spent most of the summer working on it, only to be flummoxed when the game completely consumed the 64K (expanded!) of RAM available. A year or so later I got involved in my high school's theatre program and started learning how to play electric guitar, and programming didn't feel that important anymore. So the floppy disks went into a box along with the computer and peripherals and it sat my parent's house until one day it was sold and that was that.
Let's now time-travel to the future a bit. It's 2018, and I've somehow gotten myself a career in software engineering, despite getting D's in maths and a BA in English that took five years to complete. I'm on a leave of absence, and I'm poking around
Playfic
marveling at the thousands of text adventure games written by hobbyists. This is how I learn about the existence of
Inform 7
, a modern programming language for creating text adventures ("interactive fiction" in today's parlance) that run on ported versions of the original Infocom software.
So I have an idea.
The
The Plot of the Phantom
code was gone, but I still had the original notebook of maps and objects. How fun would it be to recreate the game using the same virtual machine that Infocom used to create
Zork?
Well, not fun enough at the time I guess, because I quickly forgot about it after my leave ended.
But then: COVID. Stuck working from home, protests everywhere, wildfires turing the sky orange, a terrible election year. I needed something to escape, and that's when I pulled out that notebook started tinkering with Inform 7. I hadn't written down everything so it took some time to remember how some of the rooms and puzzles worked. I did some editing, removing some rooms, getting rid of scoring and treasure hunting, and — important! — changing the ending to be a lot less violent (I blame 80s action movies).
As I went about recreating my minature world, the backstory started to become...
meta.
The original version didn't actually have a story arc, you just had to get from one end of the dungeon to the other. Today the game has some references to the kid I was in 1984, and in some ways is a bit autobiographical. There are some new objects to examine and puzzles to explore, but the new game is largely what it was back then.
And now, it's finished.
After forty years, you can now play
The Plot of the Phantom
in your web browser
. It's pretty short, and it's not particularly difficult either, especially if you've played similar games. You can probably finish it in an hour or two.
I'm kind of
happysad
about it? It feels little bit like putting a ghost to rest.
Anyway, I enjoyed making some retro box art! Look close, there are clues.

• Nevermark 分享了自己从早期接触文本冒险游戏到后来开发复杂游戏的经历，强调了在编程和创新方面的学习经验，并对某些老游戏的遗忘表示遗憾。
• ThinkingGuy 提到在1980年代，自制文本冒险游戏是常见项目，并表示自己存档了一些未完成或未分享的游戏。
• Pet_Ant 提到了一个来自东欧的仍在开发的冒险游戏，该游戏具有复杂的因果关系和深度，但无法找到该游戏的具体信息。
• amiga386 推荐了一本关于冒险游戏编程的书，鼓励大家学习冒险游戏编程的秘诀。
• noisy_boy 和 janeway 对游戏的幽默和趣味性表示赞赏。
• matthewsinclair 分享了自己在不同硬件平台上完成游戏开发的经历。
• BryanLegend 以幽默方式提到是否是George RR Martin编写了该游戏。
• alienbaby 分享了自己使用PAWS在Amstrad PCW上开发文本冒险游戏的经历，并考虑重新挖掘出来。
• scoot 提出文本冒险游戏在第二语言学习中的应用可能性，并讨论了LLM（大型语言模型）在改善用户体验方面的潜力，认为LLM应作为理解玩家指令的翻译器而非游戏状态的仲裁者。
• ninetyninenine 进一步阐述了LLM在文本冒险游戏中的应用，认为LLM可以作为游戏状态与玩家之间的接口，保持游戏世界的一致性和结构，同时增加动态性。

补充讨论：
• 关于LLM在文本冒险游戏中的应用存在一定讨论，scoot 和 ninetyninenine 都认为LLM可以改善游戏体验，但在LLM的具体功能和角色上存在细微差别。scoot 认为LLM应仅作为翻译器，而 ninetyninenine 则建议LLM作为游戏状态的动态报告者。
• 对老游戏的遗忘和保存问题被提及，Nevermark 对 Mystery Mansion 等游戏的遗忘表示遗憾，而 ThinkingGuy 提到许多未共享的游戏可能存在于旧软盘中。
• Pet_Ant 提到的东欧冒险游戏引发了对特定深度和因果关系复杂的游戏的兴趣，但具体游戏信息不详。

争议焦点：
• LLM在文本冒险游戏中的具体应用和角色是讨论中的一个潜在争议点，虽然都认可LLM的潜力，但在其具体功能上存在不同看法。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了C语言中的指针来源（pointer provenance）问题及其对编译器别名分析和程序优化的影响。由多位专家合作推动的努力，促成了国际标准技术规范ISO/IEC TS 6010的发布，该规范为C语言的指针来源提供了明确的数学定义，解决了现有C标准中的 ambiguity。文章通过一个递归函数的例子说明了指针别名对代码优化的影响，指出如果编译器无法正确分析指针是否指向同一对象，可能会导致不理想的优化结果。因此，良好的别名分析对于现代编译器的优化至关重要。文章最后强调了如何通过正确理解和应用指针来源模型来避免优化过程中的问题。

common vision of so-called

, defining how to trace
the origins of pointer values through program execution.  Our
provenance-aware memory object model for
C

ambiguity of these aspects of the current
C
standard
. It has also
stimulated and informed discussion of provenance in the broader C,
C++, Rust, and compiler communities.
This work has finally resulted in the publication of an international
standard, Technical Specification
ISO/IEC TS
6010
(edited by
Henry
Kleynhans
, Bloomberg,
UK).  With the goal of making modern information systems safer and
more secure, this official technical specification provides direction
to all stakeholders in the industry such that they can converge their
platforms and tools.
In this article, I will try to explain what this is all about, namely
on how a provenance model for pointers interferes with alias analysis
of modern compilers. For those that are not fluent with the
terminology or the concept we have a short intro
what pointer
aliasing is all about
, a
review of existing tools to help the compiler and inherent
difficulties
and then the
proposed model
itself
. At the end there is a brief
takeaway
that explains how to generally avoid
complications and loss of optimization opportunities that could result
from mis-guided aliasing analysis.
Pointer aliasing and program optimization
We say that two pointer values
p
and
q
during the execution of a
program
alias
if they point to the same object in
memory.
[1]
To see that the question if two pointers alias
has an influence on the optimization of code, let’s consider the
following simple example of an iterative function.
[2]
It implements an approximation algorithm for the reciprocal
r := 1/a
of the value
a := *aₚ
which doesn’t use division.
// Reciprocal approximation
//
// This interface is horrific, don't use it.
// This just serves as an artificial example
// for this article.
constexpr double ε  = 0x1P-24;
constexpr double Π⁻ = 1.0 - ε;
constexpr double Π⁺ = 1.0 + ε;
void recip(double* aₚ, double* řₚ) {
for (;;) {
register double Π = (*aₚ)*(*řₚ);
if ((Π⁻ < Π) && (Π < Π⁺)) {
break;
} else {
(*řₚ) *= (2.0 - Π);
}
}
}
The function receives a pointer to a second value
ř := *řₚ
with a
rough approximation for
r
. It then iteratively approaches
r

a chosen precision
ε

a
and

into a value
Π

1.0

iteration stops. If it is not,
ř

continues.
What is interesting for our context of aliasing is that this function
has two pointer arguments that both point to a value of the same type
double
. One of these pointer targets
*řₚ
is loaded from memory,
modified and stored at each iteration. In total, the non-optimized
function as specified above in each iteration has
3 load and 1 store operations,
2 comparisons,
1 logical operation, and
3 arithmetic operations.
So loads and stores from memory make up 4 of about 10 operations in
total.
But wait, can’t this be done better? Yes, obviously, a much better
version of this could look as follows.

register double a = *aₚ;
register double ř = *řₚ;
for (;;) {
register double Π = a*ř;
if ((Π⁻ < Π) && (Π  *The functions `recip` and `recip⁺` and not equivalent.*
We didn't see this, yet, because we failed to discuss an important
feature of the original program; the pointers `aₚ` and `řₚ` may either
point
- to different objects, or
- to the same object.
Indeed, our optimized function `recip⁺` only covers the first of these
possibilities and not the second: the second case provides a
completely different algorithm for which I wouldn't know any use or
properties. But since the compiler can't know which of these cases we
have in mind (maybe both?) it cannot do an optimization that excludes
the second.[^better]
In general, loads and stores from memory are expensive operations, so
a lot of effort in modern compiler frameworks goes into so-called
alias analysis, that is in an detailed analysis of which pointers
may alias each other (or not). Such alias analysis then can be used to
mechanically prove whether a specific optimization is feasible or not.
[^better]: Any modern compiler will still do some optimization with
`recip`, but would usually not arrive at the same level of
improvement.
> *Good alias analysis of pointer targets is crucial for
> optimization in modern compilers.*

data.title: Does Form Shape Function?
data.author: lentoutcry
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了形式与功能之间的关系，特别是通过哈佛大学教授L. Mahadevan的研究。Mahadevan运用数学和物理学研究复杂生物形式和行为，如大脑褶皱和昆虫建筑，揭示物理力量、环境和具体化如何相互作用形成这些现象。他关注诸如莫比乌斯带等物体的平衡形状及其几何特性，而不仅是传统的拓扑学视角。文章还讨论了形式如何影响功能，以及功能是否迫使某些形式出现，涉及生物系统中的形态发生和社会性昆虫群落等问题。通过研究凝胶、石膏和LED灯等材料，Mahadevan试图揭示生物系统中的形式与功能关系。

• **incognito124**：对Steven Strogatz主持播客表示惊讶，侧重于对演讲者相关活动的兴趣，而非讨论演讲内容本身。

What links a Möbius strip, brain folds and termite mounds? The answer is Harvard University’s L. Mahadevan, whose career has been devoted to using mathematics and physics to explore the form and function of common phenomena.
Mahadevan, or Maha to his friends and colleagues, has long been fascinated by questions one wouldn’t normally ask — from the equilibrium shape of inert objects like a Möbius strip, to the complex factors that drive biological systems like morphogenesis or social insect colonies.
In this episode of
The Joy of Why
, Mahadevan tells co-host Steven Strogatz what inspires him to tackle these questions, and how gels, gypsum and LED lights can help uncover form and function in biological systems. He also offers some provocative thoughts about how noisy random processes might underlie our intuitions about geometry.

data.title: A rare asteroid flyby will happen soon, but NASA may be left on the sidelines
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了近地杀手小行星阿波菲斯将于2029年4月近距离飞越地球，为科学家提供了研究小行星内部的罕见机会，对行星防御具有重要意义。然而，NASA计划取消最有望跟踪阿波菲斯的OSIRIS-Apex任务，且其他替代方案也已被拒绝或搁置，这意味着NASA目前没有计划利用这一重要的小行星 encounter。文章还回顾了NASA在行星防御方面的发展历史，提到尽管有如NEO Surveyor和DART任务的进展，但仍面临资源不足和战略规划不力的挑战。专家呼吁NASA加强小行星威胁探测和防御能力开发，以有效应对未来潜在威胁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apophis小行星接近地球的可能性及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [southernplaces7] 认为虽然NASA确认Apophis小行星在即将到来的近距离飞越中不会构成威胁，但思考其撞击地球的可能性仍然是一个有趣的假设。他详细描述了如果小行星撞击陆地或海洋可能带来的灾难性后果，包括巨大动能导致的毁灭性破坏、海啸以及对全球气候和社会经济的重大影响。他还对比了不同撞击场景下的可能结果，如人口密集区域与海洋撞击的不同效应。

• [bravesoul2] 则引用了NASA的官方信息，强调Apophis小行星在未来100年内不会对地球构成威胁，并指出天文学家通过密切跟踪已排除了其在近期撞击地球的可能性。这一观点旨在平息对Apophis撞击地球的担忧，强调科学观测带来的信心。

补充讨论：
• [southernplaces7] 详细描述了小行星撞击陆地时可能产生的直接和间接影响，如瞬间形成的巨大陨石坑、冲击波以及热脉冲对生物的致命烧伤效果。他还讨论了小行星撞击海洋时可能引发的海啸及其破坏力，尽管这些效应较难精确估算。

A little less than four years from now, a killer asteroid will narrowly fly past planet Earth. This will be a celestial event visible around the world—for a few weeks, Apophis will shine among the brightest objects in the night sky.
The near miss by the large Apophis asteroid in April 2029 offers NASA a golden—and exceedingly rare—opportunity to observe such an object like this up close. Critically, the interaction between Apophis and Earth's gravitational pull will offer scientists an unprecedented chance to study the interior of an asteroid.
This is fascinating for planetary science, but it also has serious implications for planetary defense. In the future, were such an asteroid on course to strike Earth, an effective plan to deflect it would depend on knowing what the interior looks like.
"This is a remarkable opportunity," said Bobby Braun, who leads space exploration for the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, in an interview. "From a probability standpoint, there’s not going to be another chance to study a killer asteroid like this for thousands of years. Sooner or later, we’re going to need this knowledge."
But we may not get it.
NASA has some options for tracking Apophis during its flyby. However, the most promising of these, a mission named OSIRIS-Apex that breathes new life into an old spacecraft that otherwise would drift into oblivion, is slated for cancellation by the Trump White House's budget for fiscal year 2026.
Other choices, including dragging dual space probes out of storage, the Janus spacecraft, and other concepts that were submitted to NASA a year ago as part of a call for ideas, have already been rejected or simply left on the table. As a result, NASA currently has no plans to study what will be the most important asteroid encounter since the formation of the space agency.
"The world is watching," said Richard Binzel, an asteroid expert at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. "NASA needs to step up and do their job."
But will they?
A short history of planetary defense
For decades,
nearly every
public survey
asking what NASA should work on has rated planetary defense at or near the very top of the space agency's priorities. Yet for a long time, no part of NASA actually focused on finding killer asteroids or developing the technology to deflect them.
In authorization bills
dating back to 2005, Congress began mandating that NASA "detect, track, catalog, and characterize" near-Earth objects that were 140 meters in diameter or larger. Congress established a goal of finding 90 percent of these by the year 2020. (We've blown past that deadline, obviously.)
NASA had been informally studying asteroids and comets for decades but did not focus on planetary defense until 2016, when the space agency established the Planetary Defense Coordination Office. In the decade since, NASA has made some progress, identifying more than 26,000 near-Earth objects, which are defined as asteroids and comets that come within 30 million miles of our planet's orbit.
Moreover, NASA has finally funded a space mission designed specifically to look for near-Earth threats,
NEO Surveyor
, a space telescope with the goal of "finding asteroids before they find us." The $1.2 billion mission is due to launch no earlier than September 2027.
NASA also funded the
DART mission
, which launched in 2021 and impacted a 160-meter asteroid named Dimorphous a year later to demonstrate the ability to make a minor deflection.
But in a report published this week, NASA's Office of Inspector General found that despite these advances, the space agency's approach to planetary defense still faces some significant challenges. These include a lack of resources, a need for better strategic planning, and competition with NASA's more established science programs for limited funding.
A comprehensive plan to address planetary defense must include two elements, said Ed Lu, a former NASA astronaut who co-founded the B612 Foundation to protect Earth from asteroid impacts.
The first of these is the finding and detection of asteroid threats. That is being addressed both by the forthcoming NEO Surveyor and the recently completed Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which is likely to find thousands of new near-Earth threats. The challenge in the coming years will be processing all of this data, calculating orbits, and identifying threats. Lu said NASA must do a better job of being transparent in how it makes these calculations.
The second thing Lu urged NASA to do is develop a follow-up mission to DART. It was successful, he said, but DART was just an initial demonstration. Such a capability needs to be tested against a larger asteroid with different properties.
An asteroid that might look a lot like Apophis.
About Apophis
Astronomers using a telescope in Arizona found Apophis in 2004, and they were evidently fans

data.title: 1000 Days Without Drinking
data.author: hiAndrewQuinn
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了自己戒酒1000天的经历和感受。他反思了过去酗酒的行为，认为自己浪费了大约十年的时间在无节制的饮酒上，并为此感到后悔。作者提到，真正的精神康复始于你完全忘记曾经生病的感觉，不再理解过去行为的逻辑。他对比了过去酗酒的自己和现在清醒的自己，表示后者战胜了前者，并 metaphorically 提到“杀死过去以编织未来”的观点。最后，他幽默地提到死亡总是最后到来，而自己正在等待未来的到来。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：心理健康的恢复、饮酒习惯与成瘾风险、戒酒的经历与好处

不同观点：
• 关于心理健康的恢复，[eawgewag]认为真正的康复是从你彻底忘记曾经病态的情感状态开始的。他以自己从抑郁中康复的经历为例，说明经过多年后，那些情感状态不再能被清晰 recall。

• 关于饮酒习惯和成瘾风险，[matt-attack]表示自己只是适度饮酒，但担心是否有成为酒精成瘾者的风险，并询问应该注意哪些迹象。

• 关于戒酒的经历与好处，[surprisetalk]分享了自己参与“1000 Weeks Without Drinking”计划，并推荐该计划，表明长期戒酒是有益的。

• [more_corn]则表示自己五年前戒酒，并认为过去的酗酒对记忆力造成了永久性损害，后悔没有更早戒酒。

• [dnel]支持戒酒的长期益处，分享了自己1,360天戒酒的经历，并表示仍在从中获得新的自我认知。

补充讨论：
• [immibis]对[surprisetalk]提到的链接页面内容提出批评，认为该页面的逻辑有问题，尤其是关于对小罪行处以死刑作为威慑的观点，并指出作者自称为自由意志主义者，显得矛盾。

44422098.article_content:
1000 days without drinking
Add me on
LinkedIn
!
You can cite this post as a reason if you're shy.
According to Beeminder
,
today marks 1000 days since I decided to go sober.
I don’t know if it is 1000 days since my
last
drink, exactly, but it’s
certainly possible.
I feel accomplished. Indeed, the only thing I regret about reaching 1000
days now is that I ever started at all. What few promises civilizational
culture likes to toss around about alcohol being a “social lubricant”
don’t apply if you’re drinking bottom shelf vodka alone in the basement,
like I was.
And yet… I suspect
I was the kind of alcoholic who gave alcohol a bad name
.
I could have done
so much more
with the ~decade I half wasted drinking
myself into unconsciousness. Instead of accept the mantle thrust upon me
and do the basic, routine things I knew would reliably get me closer to
my goals, I decided to reach for oblivion at the low price of $20 per
week.
I have a theory, based on many years of research and practice with Anki,
that true healing from any kind of psychic illness only starts to set in
place when you start to genuinely forget what it was ever like to be ill
at all. When the actions of past-you stop making sense to current-you
from a personal standpoint. You can look back on the stupid shit you did
at 20 and say e.g. “Yeah I was so BPD then”, diagnostic papers in hand,
but that’s a different kind of
thing to being able to
reconstruct the logic that led you to take those
actions
. You have forgotten how to factor that equation. There is
something so similar to looking at death when you notice it happening.
Alcoholic me did not deserve to ‘die’ in this sense. No one does.
Regardless, he got outboxed by sober me in a fair match. He will not be
getting up any time soon. It is the way of all woken things to kill
our pasts so that our futures may be quilted.
Home
Friends of the stable sort:
alex (sbsbsb.sbs)
Death comes last to the party! Meanwhile I'm biding my time! So you can't take your own life - that's cutting in line!

data.title: Donkey Kong Country 2 and Open Bus
data.author: colejohnson66
data.article_summary:
《Donkey Kong Country 2》在旧SNES模拟器ZSNES中存在一个知名bug：某些关卡的旋转桶无法正常控制。具体表现为，当角色跳入桶中后，按方向键本应控制桶的旋转，但在ZSNES中，轻触方向键会导致桶无限旋转，直到按反方向键才会停止。这个bug使游戏难度增加，因为旋转桶常出现在尖刺等危险上方。

该问题源于ZSNES未正确模拟"开放总线"行为。这种行为发生在读取无效内存地址时，CPU会重新读取上次在数据总线上的值。SNES的CPU是65816，其复杂的内存分页和地址处理进一步增加了模拟难度。

这个问题曾在ZSNES论坛上讨论，但论坛已下线，而另一个模拟器Snes9x通过硬编码修复了此问题。ZSNES由于长期未更新（最后版本于2007年发布），该bug一直未被修复。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕6502汇编编程中的错误、开放总线（Open Bus）行为及其在不同硬件和模拟器中的表现展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **deater**：作为6502程序员，经常因为忘记在立即值前加`#`而导致错误，这种错误有时在某些机器或模拟器上不会显现，但在其他机器上会出现，特别是在演示活动（demoparty）中遇到问题时，时间压力很大。
• **anonymousiam**：最初以为"Open Bus"是一个专有名词，后来明白是指总线未连接任何设备。指出未注意到立即模式的问题，直到使用老旧模拟器时才显现出来。还提到立即模式会加快代码执行速度，这在裸机上可能重要，而在模拟器上不一定。
• **Dwedit**：提到在SNES游戏Puyo Puyo中遇到PPU开放总线的问题，在处理RetroArch的RunAhead功能时发现存档状态不匹配。
• **jackettm**：在Parallax Propeller芯片编程中也遇到类似问题，忘记写`JMP #address`而写成`JMP address`，这种错误有时能工作，直到突然出错。
• **nicetryguy**：承认自己也常犯6502汇编中的类似错误，认为这是很常见且容易犯的错误，建议在IDE中高亮`#`以减少错误。
• **userbinator**：指出"开放总线"仅存在于早期系统中，现代系统会有默认值或通过协议通知无响应。
